evidence: Cic. Brut. 92: nūlla enim rēs tantum ad dīcendum prōficit quantum scrīptiō
M-O s.v. composition, paper (school), after Egger
terms.comment: Composition in writing, Cicero’s exercise for the orator, and in the plural written works; Egger uses it of a paper written at school (Morgan–Owens). The subject set is the thema or argūmentum (see subject, a topic).
Classically careful preparation, then a written study (the elder Pliny, Gellius); see also article.
A handling of a subject (Quintilian), a treatise in the elder Pliny; Traupman’s word for an essay, beside libellus (p. 29).

evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.150: assidua ac dīligēns scrīptūra (Lewis & Short)

terms.comment: Classically the putting together of things, and in rhetoric the arrangement of words (Lewis & Short); the school sense is modern.

terms.gloss: a little book, a short piece of writing
terms.comment: The diminutive of liber: a booklet, a pamphlet, a short written piece (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: nūlla enim rēs tantum ad dīcendum prōficit quantum scrīptiō
phrases.english: for nothing does so much for speaking as writing compositions

phrases.latin: Crās tibi trādenda est scrīptiō dē Bulgariā.
phrases.english: You have to hand in an essay on Bulgaria tomorrow.
